questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. **

Delhi had been captured, ransacked and rebuilt several (1)/ times and modern Delhi is a cluster of a number (2)/ of cities spread across the metropolitan region. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Option 1)__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **'Delhi has been' **should be there in place of **'Delhi had been'**
 
• The present perfect is a verb tense which is used to show that an action has taken place once or many times before now. The present perfect is most frequently used to talk about experiences or changes that have taken place, but there are other less common uses as well.
 
• Since we are talking about Delhi the above-mentioned actions happened sometime in the past but Delhi is still evolving and is now a cluster of cities, hence the action is still in progress, therefore "has been" is the most appropriate.
 
• So, present perfect will be more accurate to use here.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ransacked **means go through (a place) stealing things and causing damage 
 
• **Cluster **means a group of similar things or people positioned or occurring closely together
 
• **Across **is a preposition which means from one side to the other of (a place, area, etc.)

​**Thus, the correct sentence is:*** **Delhi has been captured, ransacked, and rebuilt several times and modern Delhi is a cluster of a number of cities spread across the metropolitan region.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence ****given**** with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

The closure ________ the workers adversely.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Affected.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

__
 
• In the above given blank, **'affected'** will be used.
 
• The closing of a shop or factory would have a **harmful** **impact** on its workers, who will lose their jobs.
 
• **Adverse***(adjective)* - preventing success or development; harmful; unfavourable.
 
 
• For Example - Taxes are having an **adverse **effect on production.
 
 
 
• **Affected***(adjective)* - influenced or touched by an external factor.
 
 
• For Example - It gave her a strange sense of loss that **affected **her more than she wanted to admit.
 
 
 
• The sentence tells that the workers will be influenced by the closure in a harmful way.
 
• Thus, **'affected'** is the most appropriate option.

**Therefore, the correct sentence is** *The closure **affected **the workers adversely.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• Let's look at the **meaning **of the other options:- 

 
 
• **Expected** = believed that something will happen.
 
• **Effected** = caused to come into being
 
• **Accept** = believed to be correct.

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in ****correct**** order. **

Many people look down upon

P: they feel that

Q: abstract art because

R: abstractionists compose irrationally
questions.solution:
A sentence can't end with **because** => Q can't be third => rule out 3) and 4).

P can't be first since it starts with **they** and *look down upon **they** *will be grammatically incorrect. Rule out 1).

Option 2) *QPR *is the correct answer.

***Many people look down upon abstract art because they feel that abstractionists compose irrationally.***

questions.question:
A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.

She expects good news.

options.text: Good news is expected by her.
News should be good by her.
Good news was expected by her.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1315b0ed28cca1c7d8a1844355c4427c5e357e2a736f187b995f94d26e2633fc.png] **__Explanation:__**

The given sentence is given in active voice to convert it into passive voice, the following changes should be done:

 
• While converting the voice, subject, and object to change their places.
 
 
• 'Good news' is an object in an active voice that becomes the subject in the passive voice.
 
• 'She' which is a subject in the active voice becomes 'her' (objective case) object in passive voice.
 
 
 
• Simple present tense in active voice becomes (is + V₃) in passive voice.
 
• The preposition 'by' is introduced before the 'object'

**Thus, the sentence becomes: ***Good news is expected by her.*

questions.question:
A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.

“Do you write with a left hand?” she asked.

options.text: She asked whether I wrote with a left hand.
She asked that did I wrote with a left hand.
She ask if I write with my left hand.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**She asked whether I wrote with a left hand.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• The above-given sentence is a question-sentence. Such a question can be answered by saying only 'Yes' or 'No'.
 
• To make an indirect speech of such questions, the word 'if' or 'whether' will be used in indirect speech.
 
• Both the words 'if' and 'whether' can be used interchangeably.
 
• Question mark (?) will not be used in the indirect speech of interrogative sentences.
 
• The question sentence will be expressed in assertive or positive form instead of interrogative form in the indirect speech i.e. helping verb will come after subject
 
• **Present Indefinite tense **in direct speech is changed into **past indefinite tense **in indirect speech.
 
• Hence, from the above rules option 1) i.e. *She asked whether I wrote with left hand *is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph. **

I would then look

A- do some hand-holding and when they were

B- around for my colleagues to

C- not in sight, pray for divine intervention
questions.solution:
Only B can be first in the sequence. With A (*look do some) *and C (*look not*), it will be grammatically incorrect. Option 3) *BAC *is the correct answer.

***I would then look around for my colleagues to do some hand-holding and when they were not in sight, pray for divine intervention.***
